subject: Integration follow-up: SDK/auth/routing + observability hooks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Fisher <sam.fisher@acromed.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration follow-up: SDK/auth/routing + observability hooks

Hi Sam — great call today, thanks for walking through AcroMed's reranker + search flow. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single reference: 

1) Goals we heard
- Tight latency SLO on re-rank path (~50-80ms p95 for 3–5 candidate reranks)
- Auth must be compatible with your FIPS KMS and allow short-lived creds for pods
- Want structured output for entity extraction + a tool-calling hook for exact-match lookups
- Need clear observability: trace IDs, per-stage latency breakdowns, and token-level metrics in dashboards

2) SDK & auth options (recommendation)
- Use Redwood's official Node SDK (attachment: redwood-sdks.md) for fastest path; supports auto-retry and streaming.
- Auth: two viable approaches: API key (short-lived via Hashicorp Vault rotation) or mTLS with our Private offering. For your compliance needs, we'll prototype short-lived API keys backed by your KMS (we support STS-style token exchange).

3) Routing and variants
- Route user requests by priority: live-search -> reranker -> tool-calling model. We suggest a dedicated route for reranks pinned to a quantized model for cost/latency predictability.
- Fallbacks: route to a cheaper variant on capacity pressure (automatic).

4) Structured output & tool calling
- Use the SDK's structured-output mode: provide a JSON Schema for the entity extractor and a separate tool-hook for the verifier lookup.
- We'll share a short sample for the tool-calling handshake (see next message).

5) Observability (critical)
- Pass a per-request trace header: x-rw-trace-id (UUID). Redwood will surface this in Console traces.
- Recommended logging fields to capture on your side: request_id, x-rw-trace-id, route, model_name, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms_total, latency_ms_queue, latency_ms_batch, latency_ms_compute.
- We'll enable a per-route latency breakdown header in responses: X-Redwood-Latency (queue/exec/send in ms). Captured in Console and available via API.

Next steps (I propose):
- I will send an annotated SDK snippet + Postman collection (attached) you can drop into SRE's environment.
- Sam / Ana: confirm which auth path you prefer (short-lived API key vs mTLS) and provide allowlist IP ranges.
- Tech sync: 30–45m with your SRE + our infra engineer (times below).

Attachments: redwood-sdks.md, sample-postman-collection.json

Thanks — happy to pair on the tech sync.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Sam Fisher <sam.fisher@acromed.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ana Ruiz <ana@acromed.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:03:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: SDK/auth/routing + observability hooks

Thanks Marissa — really clear. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: the 50–80ms p95 is aggressive for reranking at scale. Our current baseline for a 5-candidate rerank is ~120ms p95. Can you confirm which part of the pipeline is most likely to consume time (queue vs compute)? We need to set expectations for Prod.
- Auth: procurement prefers short-lived API keys (rotated by Vault). SRE flagged mTLS as a fallback because of extra network setup.
- Region: we need this to be in us-west-2.

I'll loop Ana (SRE) into this thread — she can share allowlist ranges and SSO details. Also want to book the tech sync: Thu 03 Mar 2026 10:30 PT or Fri 04 Mar 2026 08:30 PT — which works?

Sam
CTO, AcroMed Analytics
sam.fisher@acromed.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Fisher <sam.fisher@acromed.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ana Ruiz <ana@acromed.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 09:41:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: SDK/auth/routing + observability hooks

Thanks all — quick operational notes ahead of the tech sync: 

1) Routing suggestion:
- Create two dedicated routes: rerank-prod (pinned quantized) and rerank-fallback (cheaper variant). Use request header X-RW-ROUTE to explicitly select in your service when you know latency budget.

2) Observability fields to send into your logging pipeline (in addition to x-rw-trace-id):
- rw.request_id (our unique request id)
- rw.route_name
- rw.model_id
- rw.tokens_in
- rw.tokens_out
- rw.latency.queue_ms
- rw.latency.exec_ms
- rw.latency.send_ms
- rw.status_code (proxy-level + model-level)

We'll push a sample Kibana/CloudWatch dashboard JSON to the Drive link so your SREs can import. For the demo we'll run a 5k qps-equivalent microbenchmark (burst) and show p50/p95 with and without prefix KV cache enabled.

See you on Thu 04 Mar 2026 10:30 PT. If anything changes, flag here and we'll adapt.

- Karthik
Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
